papers.what_it_is: A 2019 multi-author review (the QTFLAG consortium) of lattice gauge theory simulation with tensor networks, digital quantum simulation and analog quantum simulators on trapped ions, Rydberg atoms, cold atoms and superconducting circuits.

assertions.value: The authors state that the manuscript reviews recent results and new tools from a quantum science approach to study lattice gauge theories, covering tensor network methods and proposals for quantum simulators in trapped ions, Rydberg atoms and superconducting circuits.
quotes: In this manuscript, recent results and new tools from a quantum science approach to study lattice gauge theories are reviewed.
Then, recent proposals for the implementation of lattice gauge theory quantum simulators in diﬀerent quantum hardware are reported, e.g., trapped ions, Rydberg atoms, and superconducting circuits.
assertions.certainty_reason: The abstract states the paper's own scope.

assertions.value: The authors state, citing earlier work, that most of the hard problems in computer science can be recast as a lattice gauge theory.
quotes: Moreover, recently it has been shown that most of the hard problems in computer science can be recast as a LGT[12, 13].
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the review without its own evidence.

assertions.value: The authors state, citing earlier work, that a class of Ising Hamiltonians with long-range disordered interactions can be mapped exactly into two-dimensional lattice gauge theory.
quotes: This class of Hamiltonians can be mapped exactly into two-dimensional LGT[14].
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the review without its own evidence.

assertions.value: The authors state that universal quantum computers are still at the first development stage despite an incredibly fast development.
quotes: universal quantum computers – despite experiencing an incredibly fast development – are still at the ﬁrst development stage[4, 5].
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the review without its own evidence.

assertions.value: The authors state that for QCD at high baryon density and in out-of-equilibrium real-time evolution, importance-sampling-based Monte Carlo simulations fail due to very severe sign or complex action problems.
quotes: where importance-sampling-based Monte Carlo simulations fail due to very severe sign or complex action problems.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the review without its own evidence.

assertions.value: The authors state that immediate results with quantitative impact on particle physics are unrealistic to hope for from quantum technologies, and that a long-term investment seems timely and most interesting.
quotes: While immediate results with quantitative impact on particle physics are unrealistic to hope for, a longterm investment in the exploration of quantum technologies seems both timely and most interesting.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the review without its own evidence.

assertions.value: The authors define the Schwinger model as QED in one spatial dimension.
quotes: The Schwinger model [76, 77], i.e., QED in one spatial dimension, is arguably the simplest theory of gauge-matter interaction
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the term where it first uses it.

assertions.value: The authors state that the first DMRG study of the Schwinger model improved by orders of magnitude the precision of the ground state energy and vector particle mass gap relative to other numerical techniques, with precision decreasing fast for higher excitations.
quotes: it already improved by orders of magnitude the precision of the ground state energy and vector particle mass gap
although the precision decreased fast for higher excitations.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the review without its own evidence.

assertions.value: The authors report that for massless fermions (analytical vector value 0.5641895) the open-boundary MPS gives vector binding energy 0.56421(9) and the gauge-invariant uniform MPS gives 0.56418(2).
quotes: In the case of massless fermion, the analytical values are MV /g = 0.5641895 and MS/g = 1.12838.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the review without its own evidence.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper cites these values from earlier MPS studies; both numbers sit within about 1e-4 of the analytic value.

assertions.value: The authors report a continuum vacuum chiral condensate for massless fermions of 0.159930(8) from MPS with open boundary conditions, against the exact value 0.159929.
quotes: In the former case the exact value can be computed analytically
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the review without its own evidence.

assertions.value: The authors state that very precise results were obtained for the first and second particles in the spectrum (vector and scalar), beyond the accuracy of earlier numerical studies.
quotes: very precise results were obtained for the ﬁrst and second particles in the spectrum (respectively vector and scalar), beyond the accuracy of earlier numerical studies
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the review without its own evidence.

assertions.value: The authors state that after subtracting the UV divergence, lattice effects in the chiral condensate were found to be dominated by corrections of the form a log a.
quotes: After subtracting the UV divergence, lattice eﬀects were found to be dominated by corrections of the form a log a.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the review without its own evidence.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that these results demonstrate the feasibility of the MPS ansatz to efficiently find and describe the low-energy part of the spectrum of a lattice gauge theory in a non-perturbative manner.
quotes: These results demonstrate the feasibility of the MPS ansatz to eﬃciently ﬁnd and describe the low-energy part of the spectrum of a LGT in a non-perturbative manner.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the review without its own evidence.

assertions.value: The authors report that numerical MPS simulations of the Schwinger model ground state confirmed explicitly the predicted UV-divergent bipartite entanglement entropy scaling of 1/6 ln(ξ/a).
quotes: implying that the bipartite entanglement entropy should have a UV-divergent scaling of 1/6 ln(ξ/a)[92].
This was conﬁrmed explicitly by the numerical MPS simulations of the ground state of the Schwinger model [73, 84], as shown in ﬁgure 3a.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the review without its own evidence.

assertions.value: The authors state that the UV divergence of the entanglement requires MPS bond dimensions that grow polynomially with the inverse lattice spacing.
